name: Jason Heflin
fact: Contemporaneous confirmation of his post, and of how it began: the Herald calls him a Russellville senior and co-chairman of the Hillraiser committee, the new SGA committee President Keith Coffman introduced at the first Congress meeting of 1997-98. Heflin said the group would sit together at athletics events and sponsor drawings and contests at football, basketball, baseball, soccer and volleyball games.

name: Matt Bogard
fact: As chairman of SGA's campus improvements committee he co-authored the resolution asking Western to install two emergency telephones in the south campus car park, which Congress passed on 16 February 1999. Campus police captain Mike Wallace disputed the need for them; Bogard said the phones were a necessity because the car park is isolated and badly lit. He is still at Western in August 2004, when the Herald prints a letter from him as a graduate student from Taylorsville.

name: Jeff Baynham
fact: He helped rebuild SGA's web site in 1998, working with Brad Sweatt on a page that would post all legislation Congress passed each week and list officers' e-mail addresses. The Herald calls him a Lexington sophomore.

name: Adam Leach
fact: He was a member of Western's first mock trial team, started in spring 2001 by government professor Margaret Ellis, and is quoted on arguing a case in front of a judge as an undergraduate. The Herald calls him a Princeton senior.

name: LaJohna Brown
fact: She was the resident assistant on the third floor of Bates-Runner Hall in autumn 2001, when construction crews woke her freshmen at six in the morning. The Herald calls her a Nashville sophomore and says she had lived in South Hall her own freshman year.

name: Braden Wilson
fact: He sat on the SGA campus improvements committee that passed the bill of 5 March 2002 allocating $7,000 for new outdoor furniture in front of Cherry Hall, alongside John Bradley, Rick Upchurch and Emily Butler; the older benches were to be repainted rather than scrapped.

name: Terry Woodall
fact: He was named a Spirit Master in December 2003, and the Herald ran the congratulatory advertisement with his portrait in February 2004. In November 2004 he was at the Warren County courthouse on election night with the economics professor Brian Strow, who was standing for the county commission.

name: Troy Ransdell
fact: As a senior political science major from Louisville he wrote a signed commentary in the Herald against Western's proposed plus/minus grading system, arguing that no one had shown how it served students and that grades are not there to reward or punish. He was SGA's chief justice that year.

name: Michelle Woods
fact: She was one of two Western government students who won six-week summer internships in Washington in 2002, hers with the Washington Center's student internship clearing house. The Herald calls her a Hodgenville junior and quotes her saying she would like to be a congresswoman one day.

name: Jenny Stith
fact: She was president of the Alpha Delta Pi chapter by November 1999; the Herald calls her a Rineyville senior in its report on the Mr. Hilltopper pageant, which Alpha Delta Pi sponsored for the Ronald McDonald House. It had called her an Elizabethtown freshman in 1997.

name: Andrea Lovell
fact: She chaired SGA's campus improvements committee in 2000-01. The Herald's end-of-year review of the year in student government carries a pull quote from her, labelled campus improvements committee chairwoman, in which she says the committee set twelve goals a semester and met all of them; the story names her as a Powderly junior. The archive's officer list has her in 2000-01 only as a Congress member inferred from an award nomination.

name: Jodi Clinard-Pulley
fact: She was made a Spirit Master in April 2001, four years after her year on Congress, and the Herald photographed the ceremony. It calls her a senior from Springfield, Tennessee, which places her at Western from about 1997 to 2001.

name: Sally Eilerman
fact: She took over as co-chairwoman of the Hillraisers at the start of 1998-99 and is quoted at length on rebuilding the group, which former SGA president Keith Coffman had revived the year before. The Herald calls her a Fort Thomas junior.

name: Kyle Matthews
fact: He sat on SGA's campus improvements committee, not only academic affairs, and worked members through a proposal asking Western to put sprinkler systems in all dormitories after the Murray State fire of 18 September 1998 killed one student. The Herald calls him a Woodburn freshman and names Laura Hancock as the committee's chairwoman.

name: Larry Murphy
fact: Contemporaneous confirmation of his chairmanship: the Herald names him as the committee chairman for SGA's academic affairs while reporting the committee's work on newsletters and bulletin boards.

name: Jenny Stith
fact: Contemporaneous confirmation of her chairmanship: the Herald calls her SGA's public relations chairwoman and an Elizabethtown sophomore while reporting the committee's work on the skywalk proposal.

name: Michelle Woods
fact: As chair of SGA's academic affairs committee she sponsored the resolution asking Western to inquire into the effectiveness of its Freshman Seminar courses, which passed Congress unanimously on 19 February 2002; she then took it to the Freshman Seminar committee herself.

name: Tim Gilbert
fact: He was crowned Coming Home King in February 2001 as the Alpha Gamma Delta candidate, and was then president of Phi Delta Theta; the Herald calls him an Owensboro junior.

name: Conrad Davies
fact: In April 2000, as a Frankfort sophomore, he walked into the middle of the crowd that had gathered around the travelling evangelist Jim Gilles outside Downing University Center, put a hand on Gilles's shoulder and tried to pray with him. Gilles refused, saying his earrings prevented it.

name: Elizabeth Pemberton
fact: She was house manager of the Phi Mu chapter in 2000-01, which places her at Western from at least 1999 into 2001.
